  factory Doctor.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) => Doctor(
        id: json['id'] as int,
        title: json['title'] as String,
        lastName: json['lastName'] as String,
        firstName: json['firstName'] as String,
      );
}

// [Client] here means a PATIENT of the medical practice (vocabulary of the
// business domain, inherited from the original document) - not to be confused with
// "HTTP client", nor with this Flutter client itself!
class Client {
  final int id;
  final String title;
  final String lastName;
  final String firstName;

  Client({required this.id, required this.title, required this.lastName, required this.firstName});

  factory Client.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) => Client(
        id: json['id'] as int,
        title: json['title'] as String,
        lastName: json['lastName'] as String,
        firstName: json['firstName'] as String,
      );
}

// "light" form of a time slot, as returned by the server
// (see getMapForSlot on the NestJS side): only the fields useful for display.
class SlotJson {
  final int id;
  final int startHour;
  final int startMinute;
  final int endHour;
  final int endMinute;

  SlotJson({
    required this.id,
    required this.startHour,
    required this.startMinute,
    required this.endHour,
    required this.endMinute,
  });

  factory SlotJson.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) => SlotJson(
        id: json['id'] as int,
        startHour: json['startHour'] as int,
        startMinute: json['startMinute'] as int,
        endHour: json['endHour'] as int,
        endMinute: json['endMinute'] as int,
      );
}

// "light" form of an appointment (see getMapForAppointment on the NestJS side)
class AppointmentJson {
  final int id;
  final String day; // format "yyyy-MM-dd"
  final Client? client;
  final SlotJson? slot;

  AppointmentJson({required this.id, required this.day, required this.client, required this.slot});

  factory AppointmentJson.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) => AppointmentJson(
        id: json['id'] as int,
        day: json['day'] as String,
        client: json['client'] == null ? null : Client.fromJson(json['client'] as Map<String, dynamic>),
        slot: json['slot'] == null ? null : SlotJson.fromJson(json['slot'] as Map<String, dynamic>),
      );
}

// a slot of a doctor's schedule, free (appointment == null) or booked
class DoctorDaySlot {
  final SlotJson slot;
  final AppointmentJson? appointment;

  DoctorDaySlot({required this.slot, required this.appointment});

  factory DoctorDaySlot.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) => DoctorDaySlot(
        slot: SlotJson.fromJson(json['slot'] as Map<String, dynamic>),
        appointment: json['appointment'] == null ? null : AppointmentJson.fromJson(json['appointment'] as Map<String, dynamic>),
      );
}

// the full schedule of a doctor for a given day (see GET /getDoctorScheduleOfDay/:doctorId/:day)
class DoctorDaySchedule {
  final Doctor doctor;
  final String day;
  final List<DoctorDaySlot> slots;

  DoctorDaySchedule({required this.doctor, required this.day, required this.slots});

  factory DoctorDaySchedule.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) => DoctorDaySchedule(
        doctor: Doctor.fromJson(json['doctor'] as Map<String, dynamic>),
        day: json['day'] as String,
        slots: (json['slots'] as List<dynamic>)
            .map((e) => DoctorDaySlot.fromJson(e as Map<String, dynamic>))
            .toList(),
      );
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// authentication (see server: src/auth/, in particular login-result.model.ts)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------

// the only two roles handled by the application - exact copy of the
// [Role] type of the server (src/entities/user.entity.ts). Where TypeScript makes
// do with a union of strings ('ADMIN' | 'USER'), Dart has a
// real notion of enumeration (enum): safer (impossible to create by
// mistake a Role other than these two values), at the cost of a small explicit
// round trip with the JSON string ("ADMIN"/"USER") through
// fromString(...)/asString() below - a TypeScript "type Role =
// 'ADMIN' | 'USER'" needs no conversion at all, a JSON string IS
// already, for it, a valid value of the type.
enum Role {
  admin,
  user;

  static Role fromString(String value) {
    switch (value) {
      case 'ADMIN':
        return Role.admin;
      case 'USER':
        return Role.user;
      default:
        throw ArgumentError('Unknown role: $value');
    }
  }

  String asString() => this == Role.admin ? 'ADMIN' : 'USER';
}

// shape of the data returned by POST /login (in the usual ServerResponse<T> envelope)
class LoginResult {
  final String accessToken;
  final String login;
  final String name;
  final Role role;

  LoginResult({required this.accessToken, required this.login, required this.name, required this.role});

  factory LoginResult.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) => LoginResult(
        accessToken: json['accessToken'] as String,
        login: json['login'] as String,
        name: json['name'] as String,
        role: Role.fromString(json['role'] as String),
      );
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 11–22: The header comment details the key structural difference in this file—a [interface] [TypeScript] is only checked at COMPILE time; [Dart] KEEPS its types at runtime, hence an explicit [fromJson(...)] constructor on each class (absent from [appointment.models.ts]).
  • Lines 37–53: [class ServerResponse<T>] and its factory [fromJson(json, parseData)]—receives a FUNCTION ([parseData]) rather than relying on a simple [as ServerResponse<T>] as the [TypeScript] side (see [appointment.service.ts]): [Dart] does not know [T] at runtime (type erasure), so it cannot write [T.fromJson(...)] itself.
  • Lines 71–73: The comment notes that [Client] refers to a PATIENT from the medical practice (business domain vocabulary)—not to be confused with “HTTP client,” nor with this [Flutter] client itself, an ambiguity already noted in the three previous web variants.
  • lines 176–192: [enum Role { admin, user; ... }] — replaces the [TypeScript] string union [type Role = 'ADMIN' | 'USER'] with a REAL [Dart] enumeration, with an explicit round trip to the JSON string ([fromString]/[asString])—which is safer (it is impossible to generate an invalid [Role]), at the cost of a conversion that a string union does not need to perform.

docs.text:
Porting of [core/composables/settings.composable.ts]: keeps the URL of the [NestJS] server in memory.

// =========================================================================
// core/services/settings_service.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of core/composables/settings.composable.ts (Vue.js client of this
// course): a tiny "store" that keeps in memory the URL of the NestJS
// server.
//
// Vue.js exposes this shared state through the [provide]/[inject] pair: a
// [reactive(...)] object made only once, then read/modified in place
// by any descendant component. Flutter has neither [reactive], nor
// [provide]/[inject]: the standard equivalent of the ecosystem (and the one
// used in this course) is a ChangeNotifier - an ordinary Dart class
// which, in addition to its fields, knows how to NOTIFY its listeners
// each time a change must cause a new display, through
// the explicit call notifyListeners().
//
// The essential difference with Vue.js: [reactive(...)] wraps the object
// in a JavaScript proxy that AUTOMATICALLY detects each property
// write (store.apiBaseUrl = ... redraws by itself the components that
// read apiBaseUrl). A Dart ChangeNotifier, for its part, detects NOTHING on
// its own: it is up to the developer to call notifyListeners() after each
// modification - a little more discipline by hand, in exchange for a
// much simpler mechanism (no proxy, no "magic") to
// understand and to debug.
//
// It is the [provider] package (see pubspec.yaml and lib/main.dart) that then
// plays, around this ChangeNotifier, the role of app.provide(...) on the
// Vue.js side: it makes this single instance available to the whole widget
// subtree, through context.watch<SettingsService>() (to "read and
// resubscribe to changes", see lib/app.dart) or context.read<...>()
// (to "read once, without resubscribing").
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

class SettingsService extends ChangeNotifier {
  String _apiBaseUrl = 'http://localhost:8080';

  String get apiBaseUrl => _apiBaseUrl;

  // equivalent of "setApiBaseUrl(url: string)" on the Vue.js side - unlike
  // store.apiBaseUrl = url (a mere assignment, sufficient thanks to the
  // reactive proxy), the listeners must be explicitly notified here after
  // changing the private field.
  void setApiBaseUrl(String url) {
    if (url == _apiBaseUrl) {
      return; // avoids a useless redraw if the value has not really changed
    }
    _apiBaseUrl = url;
    notifyListeners();
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 36–39: [class SettingsService extends ChangeNotifier] with a PRIVATE field ([_apiBaseUrl]) and a public accessor ([get apiBaseUrl]) — a [ChangeNotifier] is an ORDINARY [Dart] class, with no proxy such as [reactive(...)] on the [Vue.js] side: nothing automatically detects a property read or write.
  • Lines 45–51: [setApiBaseUrl(url)] explicitly calls [notifyListeners()] AFTER updating the field — the manual step that [store.apiBaseUrl = url] did not need to perform on the [Vue.js] side, since the reactive proxy handles it on its own.

docs.title: 5.6.2. lib/core/services/auth_service.dart
docs.text:
Porting of [core/composables/auth.composable.ts]: manages the connection (POST [/login]), maintains the token [JWT], and ensures it survives a restart via [shared_preferences].

// =========================================================================
// core/services/auth_service.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of core/composables/auth.composable.ts (Vue.js client of this
// course): handles the user's login, calls POST /login, keeps
// the JWT token received (and the identity/role that come with it), and makes it
// survive a restart of the application thanks to shared_preferences -
// the cross-platform equivalent of localStorage (see below).
//
// As on the Vue.js side, this is the only other place in the application, along with
// core/services/appointment_service.dart, that talks HTTP to the server - an
// assumed exception to the rule "a single place that talks HTTP", which
// reflects, on the client side, the separation already made on the server side between
// RdvMedecinsController (business) and AuthController (authentication).
//
// IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE with Vue.js: readStoredSession() (on the Vue.js side)
// is SYNCHRONOUS - localStorage.getItem(...) returns its value
// immediately, even before the first render of the application. shared_
// preferences, for its part, is ALWAYS asynchronous (SharedPreferences.getInstance()
// returns a Future), even on the platforms where the underlying storage
// is actually a local file almost instantly read: the Dart API does not
// distinguish these cases, for consistency across ALL platforms (on
// the web, this same call relies on window.localStorage, but the Dart API
// stays asynchronous to remain identical to the other targets). Concrete
// consequence: one can no longer, as on the Vue.js side, read the already
// stored session BEFORE the widget tree is mounted - an [init()]
// explicitly asynchronous is needed, called (and AWAITED with await) from
// lib/main.dart before runApp(...), to prevent the login screen from
// "flickering" for a fraction of a second before the session is restored.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

import '../models/appointment_models.dart';
import 'settings_service.dart';

const String _storageKey = 'rdvmedecins.session';

class AuthService extends ChangeNotifier {
  // received in the constructor rather than obtained by Flutter injection: at this
  // stage (see lib/main.dart), no widget exists yet, so nothing
  // like context.read<SettingsService>() would be possible - exactly
  // the same reason as the one documented in createAuthStore(settings) on the
  // Vue.js side (src/main.ts), which also receives settingsStore as a function
  // parameter rather than through inject().
  final SettingsService settings;

  AuthService(this.settings);

  bool isLoggedIn = false;
  String? login;
  String? name;
  Role? role;
  String? accessToken;

  bool get isAdmin => role == Role.admin;

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // to be called ONLY ONCE, in lib/main.dart, BEFORE runApp(...): rereads
  // a session possibly already stored during a previous launch of
  // the application - equivalent of readStoredSession() on the Vue.js side, but
  // explicitly asynchronous (see the header of this file) rather than called
  // inside the store's constructor itself.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> init() async {
    try {
      final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
      final raw = prefs.getString(_storageKey);
      if (raw == null) {
        return; // no stored session: we stay "not logged in", default values above
      }
      final session = jsonDecode(raw) as Map<String, dynamic>;
      _applyLocalSession(
        accessToken: session['accessToken'] as String,
        login: session['login'] as String,
        name: session['name'] as String,
        role: Role.fromString(session['role'] as String),
      );
    } catch (_) {
      // shared_preferences may be unavailable, or contain a corrupted
      // value - in that case, as on the Vue.js side (try/catch of
      // readStoredSession()), we simply consider that there is no
      // session, rather than crashing the startup of the application.
    }
    // no notifyListeners() here: init() is awaited before
    // runApp(...) in lib/main.dart, so no widget is listening to this
    // ChangeNotifier yet when this method runs - notifying
    // would be useless (and would even throw an exception, a Flutter ChangeNotifier
    // forbidding notifyListeners() before having at least one
    // listener in some debug configurations).
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent of: POST /login   JSON body { login, password }
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<LoginResult> logIn(String login, String password) async {
    final httpResponse = await http.post(
      Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/login'),
      headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
      body: jsonEncode({'login': login, 'password': password}),
    );
    final envelope = ServerResponse<LoginResult>.fromJson(
      jsonDecode(httpResponse.body) as Map<String, dynamic>,
      (data) => LoginResult.fromJson(data as Map<String, dynamic>),
    );
    if (envelope.status != 0 || envelope.data == null) {
      throw Exception('Login failed');
    }
    final result = envelope.data!;
    await _applySessionAndPersist(result);
    return result;
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // logout: purely local (no server call - a JWT token is not
  // "revoked" on the server side in this port, it expires by itself after
  // JWT_EXPIRES_IN, see server .env). Called both by a click on
  // "Log out" (see lib/app.dart) and by core/http/auth_http_client.dart
  // when a protected request receives a 401.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> logOut() async {
    login = null;
    name = null;
    role = null;
    accessToken = null;
    isLoggedIn = false;
    notifyListeners();
    try {
      final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
      await prefs.remove(_storageKey);
    } catch (_) {
      // here again, a failure to clear the storage must not prevent the
      // logout on the application side, already effective above.
    }
  }

  // updates the reactive fields WITHOUT touching the storage - used by
  // init() (which has just READ the storage, no need to rewrite it).
  void _applyLocalSession({
    required String accessToken,
    required String login,
    required String name,
    required Role role,
  }) {
    this.accessToken = accessToken;
    this.login = login;
    this.name = name;
    this.role = role;
    isLoggedIn = true;
  }

  // updates the reactive fields AND persists the session - used by
  // logIn() above. Groups what applySession(...) did
  // in a single block on the Vue.js side (reactive state + localStorage written
  // together); here, the two operations are separated because the writing
  // is asynchronous (await prefs.setString(...)) whereas the update
  // of the fields must happen IMMEDIATELY and synchronously
  // (notifyListeners() must follow the assignment of the fields without waiting for
  // disk I/O) - reversing the order would needlessly delay the refresh
  // of the interface.
  Future<void> _applySessionAndPersist(LoginResult result) async {
    _applyLocalSession(
      accessToken: result.accessToken,
      login: result.login,
      name: result.name,
      role: result.role,
    );
    notifyListeners();
    try {
      final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
      await prefs.setString(
        _storageKey,
        jsonEncode({
          'accessToken': result.accessToken,
          'login': result.login,
          'name': result.name,
          'role': result.role.asString(),
        }),
      );
    } catch (_) {
      // the session remains valid IN MEMORY for this run of
      // the application even if persisting fails (quota exceeded,
      // read-only storage...) - only a future restart of
      // the application would suffer from it (the user would have to log in again).
    }
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 16–29: The header comment details the most significant difference in this file—[readStoredSession()] on the [Vue.js] side is SYNCHRONOUS; [shared_preferences] is ALWAYS asynchronous, regardless of the platform, hence an explicit [async] [init()], which is awaited by [lib/main.dart] BEFORE [runApp(...)].
  • lines 69–95: [Future<void> init() async { ... }] — reads any cached session, protected by a [try/catch] — same precaution as for [try/catch] from [readStoredSession()] on the [Vue.js] side (storage unavailable or value corrupted).
  • lines 100–116: [logIn(login, password)] — calls POST [/login] with the package [http] (the equivalent of [fetch]), throws a standard [Dart] exception ([throw Exception(...)]) in case of failure—which is later intercepted by a [try/catch] [Dart], just as the [throw new Error(...)] from [auth.composable.ts] was intercepted by a [.catch(...)] [JavaScript].
  • lines 165–190: [_applySessionAndPersist(...)] — updates the fields AND calls [notifyListeners()] BEFORE writing to [shared_preferences]: The order is deliberate—the interface must refresh IMMEDIATELY without waiting for an asynchronous disk write, whereas [applySession(...)] on the [Vue.js] side performed both operations in a single synchronous instruction.

docs.title: 5.6.3. lib/core/services/appointment_service.dart
docs.text:
Port of [core/services/appointment.service.ts]: the five business logic calls to the server, built on top of [core/http/auth_http_client.dart] (below) rather than directly on the [http] package.

// =========================================================================
// core/services/appointment_service.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of core/services/appointment.service.ts (Vue.js client of this course): the
// [Services] layer of the Flutter client - the ONLY place in the application
// (along with core/services/auth_service.dart for the login itself) that
// talks HTTP with the NestJS server.
//
// Vue.js exposes this service as a COMPOSABLE (useAppointmentService()), itself
// built on two other composables (useAuthFetch(), useSettings()).
// Flutter/Dart having neither composables nor dependency injection built
// into the language, this file becomes an ordinary CLASS again, built only
// once in lib/main.dart with its two dependencies passed to the
// constructor - exactly the same principle as core/http/auth_http_client.dart,
// and the most direct way of porting "a set of functions that
// depend on something else" when the target language offers no composable.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

import '../http/auth_http_client.dart';
import '../models/appointment_models.dart';
import 'settings_service.dart';

class AppointmentService {
  final AuthHttpClient authHttp;
  final SettingsService settings;

  AppointmentService(this.authHttp, this.settings);

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // common private function: all the server responses have the shape
  // { status, data } (see core/models/appointment_models.dart). The rule
  // "if status != 0, it is an error" is centralized HERE, only once, rather
  // than repeated in each of the methods below - exactly the
  // role of extract<T>(...) on the Vue.js side.
  //
  // [parseData] is the same kind of parameter as the one already met
  // in ServerResponse.fromJson(...) (see appointment_models.dart): the function that knows how to
  // rebuild a T from the raw JSON of the [data] field, since Dart
  // cannot do it on its own (no generic "T.fromJson(...)").
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  T _extract<T>(http.Response httpResponse, T Function(dynamic rawData) parseData) {
    final envelope = ServerResponse<T>.fromJson(
      jsonDecode(httpResponse.body) as Map<String, dynamic>,
      parseData,
    );
    if (envelope.status != 0) {
      // the server's "business" error is turned into a classic Dart
      // exception, which the calling widgets can catch with a
      // simple try/catch (see lib/app.dart) - exactly like the
      // "throw new Error(...)" of appointment.service.ts, caught by the
      // .catch(...) of src/app/App.vue.
      throw Exception('The server responded with error status ${envelope.status}');
    }
    return envelope.data as T;
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent of: GET /getAllDoctors
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<List<Doctor>> getAllDoctors() async {
    final httpResponse = await authHttp.get(Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/getAllDoctors'));
    return _extract<List<Doctor>>(
      httpResponse,
      (data) => (data as List<dynamic>).map((e) => Doctor.fromJson(e as Map<String, dynamic>)).toList(),
    );
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent of: GET /getAllClients
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<List<Client>> getAllClients() async {
    final httpResponse = await authHttp.get(Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/getAllClients'));
    return _extract<List<Client>>(
      httpResponse,
      (data) => (data as List<dynamic>).map((e) => Client.fromJson(e as Map<String, dynamic>)).toList(),
    );
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent of: GET /getDoctorScheduleOfDay/{doctorId}/{day}
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<DoctorDaySchedule> getDoctorScheduleOfDay(int doctorId, String day) async {
    final httpResponse = await authHttp.get(
      Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/getDoctorScheduleOfDay/$doctorId/$day'),
    );
    return _extract<DoctorDaySchedule>(
      httpResponse,
      (data) => DoctorDaySchedule.fromJson(data as Map<String, dynamic>),
    );
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent of: POST /addAppointment   JSON body { day, clientId, slotId }
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<AppointmentJson> addAppointment(String day, int clientId, int slotId) async {
    final httpResponse = await authHttp.post(
      Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/addAppointment'),
      body: jsonEncode({'day': day, 'clientId': clientId, 'slotId': slotId}),
    );
    return _extract<AppointmentJson>(httpResponse, (data) => AppointmentJson.fromJson(data as Map<String, dynamic>));
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent of: POST /deleteAppointment   JSON body { appointmentId }
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> deleteAppointment(int appointmentId) async {
    final httpResponse = await authHttp.post(
      Uri.parse('${settings.apiBaseUrl}/deleteAppointment'),
      body: jsonEncode({'appointmentId': appointmentId}),
    );
    _extract<Object?>(httpResponse, (data) => data);
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 27–31: [class AppointmentService { final AuthHttpClient authHttp; final SettingsService settings; AppointmentService(this.authHttp, this.settings); }] — reverts to an ORDINARY CLASS, constructed once in [lib/main.dart] with its dependencies passed to the constructor, whereas [Vue.js] used a COMPOSABLE, [useAppointmentService()], which were themselves built from two other composables.
  • Lines 45–59: [T _extract<T>(httpResponse, parseData)]—centralizes, just once, the rule “if [status != 0], it’s an error,” exactly the role of [extract<T>(...)] on the [Vue.js] side—the parameter [parseData] is the same type of function already encountered in [ServerResponse.fromJson(...)].
  • Lines 99–105: [addAppointment(day, clientId, slotId)] — [jsonEncode({...})] constructs the body JSON of the request POST, the equivalent [Dart] of [JSON.stringify({...})] on the [Vue.js] side.
  • Lines 110–116: [Future<void> deleteAppointment(int appointmentId) async { ... }] — calls [_extract<Object?>(...)] without using its result: The server returns [ServerResponse.ok(null)] for this route, so there is nothing more specific to specify—the same choice as [extract<null>(httpResponse)] on the [Vue.js] side.

docs.title: 5.7.1. lib/core/http/auth_http_client.dart
docs.text:
Port of [core/interceptors/auth.interceptor.ts]: adds the token [JWT] to every protected request, logs the user out on a 401 response.

// =========================================================================
// core/http/auth_http_client.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of core/interceptors/auth.interceptor.ts (Vue.js client of this
// course). This file does two things, exactly like its
// Vue.js counterpart (itself a port of the Angular and React clients):
//   1. adds the "Authorization: Bearer <token>" header to each request, if
//      the user is logged in (see AuthService.accessToken);
//   2. if the server answers 401 (token missing, invalid or expired),
//      cleanly logs the user out on the client side.
//
// [fetch] (used on the Vue.js and React side) and Angular's [HttpClient] have
// no DIRECT equivalent in Dart: the [http] package (see pubspec.yaml)
// provides free functions (http.get(...), http.post(...)) rather
// than an object to intercept globally. The port nevertheless remains faithful
// in SPIRIT to useAuthFetch(): rather than a composable function returning
// an "enhanced fetch", a REAL CLASS is written here, [AuthHttpClient],
// whose get(...)/post(...) methods play exactly the same role -
// any code that wants to talk to the server (here, only
// core/services/appointment_service.dart) calls THESE methods rather than the
// http package directly.
//
// Writing a class rather than a composable function is a natural
// choice in Dart/Flutter: unlike a Vue.js <script setup> (which
// runs only once per component instance, see the comment of
// auth.interceptor.ts), a ChangeNotifier or a Dart service class
// has no "body executed at each render" to be wary of -
// so no equivalent of useCallback() is needed here either,
// but for a different reason: there is simply no
// function "recreated at each render" in the first place, the class being
// built only once by lib/main.dart (see below).
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:async' show unawaited;

import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;

import '../services/auth_service.dart';

class AuthHttpClient {
  final AuthService auth;
  final http.Client _client = http.Client();

  AuthHttpClient(this.auth);

  Future<http.Response> get(Uri url) => _send(() => _client.get(url, headers: _headers()));

  Future<http.Response> post(Uri url, {required Object body}) => _send(
        () => _client.post(
          url,
          headers: {..._headers(), 'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
          body: body,
        ),
      );

  // builds the headers common to every protected request - the equivalent
  // of the "new Headers(options.headers); if (auth.accessToken) {...}" on the
  // Vue.js side, but as a simple Map<String, String> (the type
  // expected by the http package, simpler here than a Headers class).
  Map<String, String> _headers() {
    final accessToken = auth.accessToken;
    return accessToken == null ? {} : {'Authorization': 'Bearer $accessToken'};
  }

  // factors out what get(...) and post(...) have in common: run the HTTP
  // call then, if the response is 401, log the user out - the
  // [call] function received as parameter plays the role of the "...options"
  // passed by fetch(path, { ...options, headers }) on the
  // Vue.js side: at this point we do not know yet whether it is a GET
  // or a POST, only that it must be run and its response examined.
  Future<http.Response> _send(Future<http.Response> Function() call) async {
    final response = await call();
    // a 401 during a session means that the token is no longer valid
    // (expired, or server restarted): the client is cleanly logged out
    // rather than leaving the application in an inconsistent state (logged in
    // in appearance, but with no request succeeding anymore). There is
    // no "await" on logOut(): the HTTP response (even an error one)
    // must be returned to the caller without waiting for the end of the clearing of
    // the local storage, which completes on its side in the background.
    if (response.statusCode == 401) {
      unawaited(auth.logOut());
    }
    return response;
  }
}

Let's comment on this code:

  • Lines 12–31: The header comment explains the choice of a CLASS ([AuthHttpClient]) over a composable—[fetch] ([Vue.js]/[React]) and [HttpClient] ([Angular]) have no direct equivalent in [Dart]; the [http] package provides standalone functions rather than a single object to be intercepted globally.
  • lines 46–54: [get(...)]/[post(...)]—the only two methods that [appointment_service.dart] calls; it never calls the [http] package directly.
  • Lines 60–63: [_headers()] — constructs [{'Authorization': 'Bearer $accessToken'}] if the user is logged in; this is the equivalent of [new Headers(options.headers); if (auth.accessToken) {...}] on the [Vue.js] side, but in the form of a simple [Map<String, String>].
  • Lines 71–84: [_send(call)] — factors out what [get(...)] and [post(...)] have in common; [unawaited(auth.logOut())] EXPLICITLY documents that we choose not to wait for [Future] — the response HTTP (even if it contains an error) must be returned to the caller without waiting for the local storage purge to complete.

docs.title: 5.8.1. lib/core/i18n/translations_service.dart
docs.text:
MERGED port of [src/i18n.ts] AND of [core/composables/language.composable.ts]: the French/English interface switching, reimplemented without a third-party library (see the header comment in the file for the reason behind this choice).

// =========================================================================
// core/i18n/translations_service.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MERGED port of src/i18n.ts (vue-i18n configuration) AND of
// core/composables/language.composable.ts (Vue.js client of this course).
// Vue.js separates the two because vue-i18n, a third-party library already
// rich in features (pluralization, date/number formats...),
// does all the actual translation work; language.composable.ts
// merely adds to it the storage of the language choice in
// localStorage. Flutter has no direct equivalent of vue-i18n/react-
// i18next/@ngx-translate/core installed by default: rather than adding
// an extra dependency, this file reimplements in a few
// lines exactly the subset used by this course - a
// dictionary with dotted keys ("LOGIN.TITLE") and a t(key) function.
//
// IMPORTANT PLATFORM DIFFERENCE (see also Chapter "Porting
// the application to mobile, desktop and web"): src/i18n.ts fetches
// each dictionary with a fetch("/i18n/{language}.json") - a relative
// URL, which assumes a WEB SERVER serving the client's files
// (Vite in development, a static server once built). A
// mobile or desktop Flutter application has NO WEB SERVER serving it
// : the code AND its static resources (here, the JSON files) are
// EMBEDDED together in a single package installed on the device (.apk,
// .app, .exe...). This is why this file uses rootBundle.loadString(...)
// - the Flutter API that reads a file declared in the [assets] section of
// pubspec.yaml directly from this package - rather than a network call.
// On the web target, rootBundle relies behind the scenes on a real HTTP
// request to the files published next to the application, but this detail
// remains invisible here: the SAME Dart code works, without any platform
// condition, on the 3 environments - exactly the central argument of
// this chapter.
// =========================================================================

import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart' show rootBundle, ServicesBinding;
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

const String _storageKey = 'rdvmedecins.language';
final String _defaultLanguage = ServicesBinding.instance.platformDispatcher.locale.languageCode == 'fr' ? 'fr' : 'en';

class TranslationsService extends ChangeNotifier {
  String currentLanguage = _defaultLanguage;

  // dictionaries already loaded (avoids rereading an asset file already seen
  // during the session) - same optimization as loadedDictionaries on the
  // Vue.js side (src/i18n.ts), but here the decoded dictionary itself is kept
  // rather than a simple Set of languages already seen: Vue.js could make do
  // with a Set because vue-i18n ITSELF keeps the loaded dictionaries
  // in memory (setLocaleMessage); having no equivalent
  // library here, this cache role must be held directly by this
  // file.
  final Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>> _dictionaries = {};

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // to be called ONLY ONCE, in lib/main.dart, BEFORE runApp(...):
  // restores the language stored during a previous launch (if there is
  // one) and loads its dictionary - equivalent of the final block of
  // createLanguageStore() on the Vue.js side (the reading of savedLanguage in
  // localStorage), but made explicitly asynchronous for the same
  // reasons already documented in core/services/auth_service.dart
  // (shared_preferences is ALWAYS asynchronous, unlike
  // localStorage).
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> init() async {
    String startLanguage = _defaultLanguage;
    try {
      final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
      startLanguage = prefs.getString(_storageKey) ?? _defaultLanguage;
    } catch (_) {
      // no readable preference: start in the default language (English, or
      // French on a French device), as on the Vue.js side.
    }
    await _loadDictionary(startLanguage);
    currentLanguage = startLanguage;
    // no notifyListeners() here, for the same reason as in
    // AuthService.init(): this method is awaited before
    // runApp(...), so no widget is listening to this ChangeNotifier yet.
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent of: changeLanguage(language) on the Vue.js side (triggered by the
  // FR/EN buttons of lib/app.dart, see later in this chapter).
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> changeLanguage(String language) async {
    if (language == currentLanguage) {
      return;
    }
    await _loadDictionary(language);
    currentLanguage = language;
    notifyListeners(); // here, on the other hand, the application is already running: we do notify
    try {
      final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
      await prefs.setString(_storageKey, language);
    } catch (_) {
      // the language change remains effective for this run even if
      // storing it fails - only a future restart would suffer from it.
    }
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // equivalent of: loadDictionary(language) on the Vue.js side - same
  // caching principle (loadedDictionaries), but reading an embedded
  // asset rather than a network fetch() (see the header of this file).
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Future<void> _loadDictionary(String language) async {
    if (_dictionaries.containsKey(language)) {
      return; // already loaded during a previous language change
    }
    final content = await rootBundle.loadString('assets/i18n/$language.json');
    _dictionaries[language] = jsonDecode(content) as Map<String, dynamic>;
  }

  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  // the translation function itself - called t('LOGIN.TITLE') from
  // the widgets (see lib/features/...), exactly like t('LOGIN.TITLE')
  // on the Vue.js side (useI18n().t). The key is "dotted" (a dot separates
  // each level): so we go down into the nested JSON dictionary one
  // segment at a time, rather than flattening the dictionary once and
  // for all as vue-i18n does internally - a choice that remains
  // largely sufficient for the size of these two dictionaries.
  // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  String t(String key) {
    final dictionary = _dictionaries[currentLanguage];
    if (dictionary == null) {
      return key; // dictionary not loaded yet: the key itself is displayed, as a last resort
    }
    dynamic currentValue = dictionary;
    for (final segment in key.split('.')) {
      if (currentValue is Map<String, dynamic> && currentValue.containsKey(segment)) {
        currentValue = currentValue[segment];
      } else {
        return key; // key not found: same fallback as above
      }
    }
    return currentValue is String ? currentValue : key;
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • Lines 16–31: The header comment details the most important PLATFORM DIFFERENCE of this entire client — [src/i18n.ts] retrieves each dictionary via [fetch("/i18n/{language}.json")], a URL that relies on a WEB SERVER; a mobile or desktop application does not have one, hence [rootBundle.loadString(...)] rather than a network call—the same code works, regardless of platform, on all three environments (see Chapter 5).
  • lines 66–80: [init()] — restores the saved language (or the default language: English, or French on a French device) and loads its dictionary; Like [AuthService.init()], there is no [notifyListeners()] here (no widget is listening to this [ChangeNotifier] at this stage).
  • lines 107–113: [_loadDictionary(language)] — the same caching principle as [loadedDictionaries] on the [Vue.js] side, but it directly stores the decoded dictionary rather than a simple [Set] of previously seen languages: [vue-i18n] kept the dictionaries in memory ([setLocaleMessage]); here, this caching role must be handled directly by this file.
  • Lines 124–138: [String t(String key) { ... }] — traverses the nested dictionary JSON one segment at a time ([key.split('.')]), rather than flattening the dictionary once and for all as [vue-i18n] does internally—a choice that is more than sufficient for the size of these two dictionaries.

docs.title: 5.9.1. lib/features/login/login_page.dart
docs.text:
Porting [src/app/features/login/Login.vue]: the login screen.

// =========================================================================
// features/login/login_page.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of src/app/features/login/Login.vue (Vue.js client of this course):
// the login screen. Like its Vue.js counterpart, this widget knows
// nothing about the schedule or the appointments: it merely collects a
// (login, password) pair, passes it to AuthService.logIn(...),
// and displays a possible error.
//
// STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE with Vue.js: Login.vue declares its local state
// (login, password, submitting, error) with simple ref(...) - Vue.js
// then automatically "redraws" the <template> when one of these refs
// changes, WITHOUT any notion of "widget with or without state". Flutter distinguishes
// explicitly two kinds of widgets: StatelessWidget (nothing ever changes
// after construction) and StatefulWidget (owns a mutable state,
// and knows how to redraw itself through setState(...)). This component needs to
// remember what the user types AND to know how to redraw itself when
// submitting/error change: so it is a StatefulWidget - the
// LoginPage class below ONLY declares createState(), all the state and
// all the logic live in _LoginPageState, the associated "twin"
// class.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../../core/i18n/translations_service.dart';
import '../../core/services/auth_service.dart';

class LoginPage extends StatelessWidget {
  const LoginPage({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return const _LoginForm();
  }
}

class _LoginForm extends StatefulWidget {
  const _LoginForm();

  @override
  State<_LoginForm> createState() => _LoginFormState();
}

class _LoginFormState extends State<_LoginForm> {
  // TextEditingController: unlike v-model="login" on the Vue.js side
  // (which directly binds a field to a ref, both ways, in a
  // single attribute), Flutter has no two-way binding built into
  // the TextField widget - one must explicitly own a controller,
  // read it (controller.text) and RELEASE it (dispose()) once the widget is
  // destroyed, see dispose() below. It is more verbose to write once,
  // but makes explicit a lifecycle (creation -> reading -> release
  // of resources) that Vue.js manages itself behind the scenes for a ref.
  final TextEditingController _loginController = TextEditingController();
  final TextEditingController _passwordController = TextEditingController();

  bool _submitting = false;
  String? _error;

  @override
  void dispose() {
    // releases the resources associated with the controllers - forgetting this
    // would cause a memory leak each time this screen was
    // recreated. Vue.js, whose ref() are simple JavaScript objects
    // collected by the garbage collector like any other object,
    // has no such step to plan for.
    _loginController.dispose();
    _passwordController.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  Future<void> _onSubmit() async {
    final login = _loginController.text.trim();
    final password = _passwordController.text;
    if (login.isEmpty || password.isEmpty) {
      return;
    }
    setState(() {
      _error = null;
      _submitting = true;
    });
    try {
      // context.read<AuthService>(): a "one-time" read, WITHOUT resubscribing
      // to future changes (unlike context.watch<...>(), see
      // lib/app.dart) - exactly suited to a one-off call triggered by
      // a user action, rather than to a display that must
      // stay up to date. It is the Flutter/provider equivalent of
      // "const auth = useAuth();" on the Vue.js side, where auth.logIn(...) is
      // simply called without any particular distinction (Vue.js does not have
      // this one-time-read / resubscription distinction: useAuth() always returns
      // the same reactive object, whatever use is made of it).
      await context.read<AuthService>().logIn(login, password);
      if (!mounted) return; // the widget may have been destroyed while waiting for the server
      setState(() => _submitting = false);
    } catch (_) {
      if (!mounted) return;
      setState(() {
        _submitting = false;
        _error = 'LOGIN.ERROR';
      });
    }
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    // context.watch<TranslationsService>(): unlike
    // context.read<AuthService>() used in _onSubmit() above, we
    // want HERE this widget to redraw itself automatically if the language
    // changes (FR/EN buttons of lib/app.dart) - watch() subscribes to
    // future changes, where read() merely does a one-off read.
    final t = context.watch<TranslationsService>().t;

    return Center(
      child: ConstrainedBox(
        constraints: const BoxConstraints(maxWidth: 420),
        child: Card(
          child: Padding(
            padding: const EdgeInsets.all(24),
            // Form groups the fields and allows submitting by pressing
            // "Enter" from any of them (onFieldSubmitted
            // below) - the equivalent of the <form @submit.prevent="onSubmit">
            // of Login.vue: Enter in a field AND a click on the button
            // both trigger the same onSubmit().
            child: Column(
              mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
              crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
              children: [
                Text(t('LOGIN.TITLE'), style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleLarge),
                const SizedBox(height: 16),
                if (_error != null) ...[
                  Container(
                    padding: const EdgeInsets.all(8),
                    decoration: BoxDecoration(
                      color: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.errorContainer,
                      borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(4),
                    ),
                    child: Text(
                      t(_error!),
                      style: TextStyle(color: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.onErrorContainer),
                    ),
                  ),
                  const SizedBox(height: 16),
                ],
                TextField(
                  controller: _loginController,
                  decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: t('LOGIN.LOGIN_LABEL')),
                  textInputAction: TextInputAction.next,
                ),
                const SizedBox(height: 12),
                TextField(
                  controller: _passwordController,
                  decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: t('LOGIN.PASSWORD_LABEL')),
                  obscureText: true,
                  textInputAction: TextInputAction.done,
                  // onSubmitted: triggered by the "Enter" key (or its
                  // mobile virtual keyboard equivalent) - the counterpart of
                  // @submit.prevent placed on the <form> tag on the Vue.js side,
                  // here placed directly on the LAST field of the form.
                  onSubmitted: (_) => _onSubmit(),
                ),
                const SizedBox(height: 20),
                FilledButton(
                  onPressed: _submitting ? null : _onSubmit,
                  child: Text(_submitting ? t('LOGIN.SUBMITTING') : t('LOGIN.SUBMIT')),
                ),
                const SizedBox(height: 16),
                Text(
                  '${t('LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS_PREFIX')} admin / admin ${t('LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS_ADMIN')} '
                  '${t('LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS_OR')} user / user ${t('LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS_USER')}.',
                  style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.bodySmall,
                ),
              ],
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 39–44: [LoginPage] (a simple [StatelessWidget] front-end) delegates EVERYTHING to [_LoginForm]/[_LoginFormState] — the header comment explains why this screen, which must store what the user types AND redraw itself when [_submitting]/[_error] change, CANNOT simply be [StatelessWidget], unlike [Login.vue], where [ref(...)] makes no such distinction.
  • lines 55–56: [final TextEditingController _loginController = TextEditingController();] — replaces [v-model="login"]: no built-in bidirectional link in [TextField]; a controller must be explicitly specified.
  • lines 61–71: [dispose() { _loginController.dispose(); _passwordController.dispose(); ... }] — releases both controllers; an omission here would cause a memory leak every time this screen is recreated, a step that [Vue.js] does not need to account for (its [ref()] objects are simply collected by the garbage collector).
  • lines 93–102: [await context.read<AuthService>().logIn(login, password);] within a [try/catch] — [context.read<...>()] (one-time read, WITHOUT resubscription) rather than [context.watch<...>()] (see [lib/app.dart]), which is well-suited for a one-time call triggered by a user action.
  • Line 160: [onSubmitted: (_) => _onSubmit(),] placed on the LAST field (password) — the counterpart to [@submit.prevent="onSubmit"], which is set on the [<form>] tag on the [Vue.js] side: Pressing Enter in the field AND clicking the button both trigger the same [_onSubmit()].

docs.title: 5.9.2. lib/features/doctor_day_picker/doctor_day_picker.dart
docs.text:
Porting of [src/app/features/doctor-day-picker/DoctorDayPicker.vue]: Select a doctor and a date, then request to view their schedule.

// =========================================================================
// features/doctor_day_picker/doctor_day_picker.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of src/app/features/doctor-day-picker/DoctorDayPicker.vue (Vue.js
// client of this course): the widget used to choose a doctor and a
// day, then to ask to see their schedule.
//
// A Vue.js [defineProps]/[defineEmits] (props as inputs, events as
// outputs) becomes here, very directly, a Dart CONSTRUCTOR: the props
// are the named parameters of the constructor (doctors, onSearch), and
// "emitting an event" simply becomes CALLING the function received as
// parameter - exactly the choice already made by the React client of this
// course (a function prop, onSearch), rather than the explicit
// [defineEmits] declaration specific to Vue.js. Flutter, like React, makes
// NO syntactic distinction between "normal prop" and "prop used to
// notify the parent": it is a function like any other, passed by the
// parent (see lib/app.dart) when building this widget.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:intl/intl.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../../core/i18n/translations_service.dart';
import '../../core/models/appointment_models.dart';

// "yyyy-MM-dd" format - the same date format as on the Vue.js side
// (new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)), but built here explicitly
// through the intl package rather than by string slicing: Dart's DateTime
// has no built-in toISOString() method.
final DateFormat _dayFormat = DateFormat('yyyy-MM-dd');

class DoctorDayPicker extends StatefulWidget {
  final List<Doctor> doctors;

  // onSearch(doctorId, day): the direct equivalent of
  // "search: [criteria: { doctorId: number; day: string }]" on the
  // Vue.js side - here, two positional parameters rather than a single object
  // {doctorId, day}, a choice as valid as the other in Dart.
  final void Function(int doctorId, String day) onSearch;

  const DoctorDayPicker({super.key, required this.doctors, required this.onSearch});

  @override
  State<DoctorDayPicker> createState() => _DoctorDayPickerState();
}

class _DoctorDayPickerState extends State<DoctorDayPicker> {
  // state purely local to this widget (what is selected in the menus,
  // as long as the user has not clicked the button) - the direct
  // equivalent of selectedDoctorId/selectedDay on the Vue.js side, as
  // simple fields of _DoctorDayPickerState rather than ref(...): a
  // Flutter StatefulWidget needs no particular "wrapping" for
  // a local field, setState(...) (see _onDoctorChoice below) is enough to
  // signal that a redraw is needed.
  int? _selectedDoctorId;
  DateTime _selectedDay = DateTime.now();

  Future<void> _pickDay() async {
    // Flutter has no direct equivalent of <input type="date"> (a date
    // input widget NATIVE TO THE BROWSER, which Vue.js could
    // benefit from on the web): on the 3 environments targeted by this client
    // (mobile, desktop, web), it is Flutter ITSELF that draws the
    // date picker (showDatePicker(...) below) - a Material
    // widget, identical in appearance on the 3 targets. It is a
    // very concrete illustration of the promise "a single code base for 3
    // environments": where Vue.js relied on a building block of the
    // browser (absent on mobile and desktop), Flutter provides its
    // own building block, available EVERYWHERE.
    final picked = await showDatePicker(
      context: context,
      initialDate: _selectedDay,
      firstDate: DateTime(2020),
      lastDate: DateTime(2100),
    );
    if (picked != null) {
      setState(() => _selectedDay = picked);
    }
  }

  void _onSearchClick() {
    final doctorId = _selectedDoctorId;
    if (doctorId == null) {
      return; // the button is disabled anyway in this case (see build() below)
    }
    // widget.onSearch(...): the function received from the parent is called -
    // exactly the equivalent of emit('search', ...) on the Vue.js side, or of
    // the call of the onSearch(...) prop on the React side. The "widget."
    // prefix is needed here because _DoctorDayPickerState is a class
    // SEPARATE from DoctorDayPicker (see the header of lib/features/login/login_page.dart
    // for the reason for this State/Widget separation specific to Flutter):
    // this is how, from the state, one accesses the parameters of the widget that
    // owns it.
    widget.onSearch(doctorId, _dayFormat.format(_selectedDay));
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final t = context.watch<TranslationsService>().t;

    // The three fields are built ONLY ONCE here, then laid out by
    // the LayoutBuilder further down: side by side (Row) on a wide screen,
    // stacked (Column) on a narrow screen. A phone in portrait mode is only
    // about 360 pixels wide: three fields in a row would each have
    // only about a hundred pixels there and would overflow.
    //
    // DropdownButtonFormField<int>: the Flutter equivalent of an
    // HTML <select> - unlike v-model="selectedDoctorId"
    // on the Vue.js side (a single two-way binding), Flutter
    // explicitly separates "displayed value" (value:) and "reaction
    // to a change" (onChanged:), in the manner of React
    // (:value + @change) already compared in the original .vue
    // file.
    final doctorField = DropdownButtonFormField<int>(
      // isExpanded: the label takes the whole available width (and is
      // cleanly truncated if it is too long) instead of overflowing.
      isExpanded: true,
      decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: t('DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DOCTOR_LABEL')),
      value: _selectedDoctorId,
      hint: Text(t('DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.CHOOSE_DOCTOR')),
      // .map(...).toList(): the Flutter equivalent of
      // v-for="doctor in doctors" :key="doctor.id" - here,
      // the "stable" identifier (:key on the Vue.js side) is simply
      // the [value:] of each DropdownMenuItem (doctor.id), which
      // Flutter itself uses to know which one is
      // currently selected.
      items: widget.doctors
          .map(
            (doctor) => DropdownMenuItem(
              value: doctor.id,
              child: Text('${doctor.title} ${doctor.firstName} ${doctor.lastName}'),
            ),
          )
          .toList(),
      onChanged: (id) => setState(() => _selectedDoctorId = id),
    );

    // InkWell: makes the whole area "clickable" - a tap
    // anywhere on it opens the date picker
    // (_pickDay above). It is a rebuilding, by
    // hand, of what the browser offered "for free" with
    // <input type="date" v-model="selectedDay"> on the Vue.js side.
    // InputDecorator (rather than a "disguised" TextField) displays
    // the date without owning a TextEditingController - there is
    // NOTHING to type on the keyboard here, only a value to
    // display and a tap to intercept: no need for the
    // create/dispose lifecycle already met in
    // lib/features/login/login_page.dart for a really editable field.
    final dayField = InkWell(
      onTap: _pickDay,
      child: InputDecorator(
        decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: t('DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DAY_LABEL')),
        child: Text(_dayFormat.format(_selectedDay)),
      ),
    );

    final scheduleButton = FilledButton(
      onPressed: _selectedDoctorId == null ? null : _onSearchClick,
      child: Text(t('DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.VIEW_SCHEDULE')),
    );

    return Card(
      child: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        // LayoutBuilder: calls its builder with the width ACTUALLY
        // available at this place of the tree (constraints.maxWidth), and
        // calls it again if it changes (screen rotation, resizing
        // of the window) - so the layout adapts by itself.
        child: LayoutBuilder(
          builder: (context, constraints) {
            if (constraints.maxWidth < 600) {
              return Column(
                crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
                children: [
                  doctorField,
                  const SizedBox(height: 12),
                  dayField,
                  const SizedBox(height: 12),
                  scheduleButton,
                ],
              );
            }
            return Row(
              crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.end,
              children: [
                Expanded(flex: 5, child: doctorField),
                const SizedBox(width: 12),
                Expanded(flex: 4, child: dayField),
                const SizedBox(width: 12),
                Expanded(flex: 3, child: scheduleButton),
              ],
            );
          },
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 59–79: [_pickDay()] calls [showDatePicker(...)]—a very concrete illustration of the promise “a single code for three environments”: whereas [Vue.js] relied on [<input type="date">], a NATIVE building block of the BROWSER (missing on mobile and desktop), [Flutter] renders ITSELF a selector that is a [Material] widget that is strictly identical across all three targets.
  • Lines 114–136: [DropdownButtonFormField<int>(value: _selectedDoctorId, ..., onChanged: (id) => setState(() => _selectedDoctorId = id))] — replaces [v-model="selectedDoctorId"] with an explicit pair [value:]/[onChanged:], similar to the pair [:value]/[@change] already encountered in connection with [React] in this course.
  • lines 149–155: [InkWell(onTap: _pickDay, child: InputDecorator(...))] — manually reconstructed from what the browser provided “for free” with [<input type="date">]; [InputDecorator] (rather than a “disguised” [TextField]) displays the date WITHOUT a [TextEditingController].
  • Lines 169–194: [LayoutBuilder(builder: (context, constraints) { ... })] — the response from [Flutter] to a screen of unknown width: [builder] receives the width actually available at that location ([constraints.maxWidth]) and is called again if it changes (screen rotation, window resizing). Below 600 pixels—a phone in portrait mode is only about 360 pixels wide—the three fields are STACKED within a [Column]; above that, they remain side by side within a [Row]. The three fields are constructed once, earlier on, in the variables [doctorField], [dayField], and [scheduleButton]: only their layout changes. With just the [Row] from the first version, each field would have had only about a hundred pixels on a phone in portrait mode, and the content would have overflowed (the yellow and black banner “RIGHT OVERFLOWED BY … PIXELS” in debug mode); [isExpanded: true] in the drop-down list prevents the same overflow for a long doctor’s name.

docs.title: 5.9.3. lib/features/schedule/schedule_view.dart
docs.text:
Port of [src/app/features/schedule/Schedule.vue]: a doctor’s schedule for a given day—available slots (“Book” button) or booked slots (patient + “Cancel” button).

// =========================================================================
// features/schedule/schedule_view.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of src/app/features/schedule/Schedule.vue (Vue.js client of this
// course): displays the schedule of a doctor for a given day - the list of
// their time slots, each one being free ("Book" button) or booked
// (patient's name + "Cancel" button).
//
// Since authentication was added, this widget also receives
// canEdit: when false (USER role), the "Book"/"Cancel" buttons
// disappear - the schedule can still be viewed, but read-only (the
// server would anyway refuse these actions to a USER, 403 Forbidden,
// see RolesGuard on the server side).
//
// [v-if]/[v-else] and [v-for] (Vue.js) become ORDINARY Dart expressions
// here: Flutter, like React before it (see the comment of
// Schedule.vue), knows NO "template language" separate from the
// programming language - const/if/for and the ?./?? operators of normal Dart
// are enough to express conditions and lists, directly in the
// build(...) method below.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../../core/i18n/translations_service.dart';
import '../../core/models/appointment_models.dart';

class ScheduleView extends StatelessWidget {
  final DoctorDaySchedule? schedule;
  final bool canEdit;
  final void Function(SlotJson slot) onBook;
  final void Function(AppointmentJson appointment) onCancel;

  const ScheduleView({
    super.key,
    required this.schedule,
    required this.canEdit,
    required this.onBook,
    required this.onCancel,
  });

  // small formatting utility function, "8:05" rather than "8:5" -
  // identical in spirit to formatTime(...) on the Vue.js side.
  static String _formatTime(int h, int m) => '$h:${m.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}';

  void _onSlotClick(DoctorDaySlot daySlot) {
    if (!canEdit) {
      return; // the button is not displayed anyway in this case (see build() below)
    }
    final appointment = daySlot.appointment;
    if (appointment == null) {
      onBook(daySlot.slot); // free slot: offer to book it
    } else {
      onCancel(appointment); // slot already booked: offer to cancel the existing appointment
    }
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final t = context.watch<TranslationsService>().t;
    final schedule = this.schedule;

    if (schedule == null) {
      return Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(vertical: 24),
        child: Text(
          t('SCHEDULE.EMPTY_STATE'),
          style: TextStyle(color: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.outline),
        ),
      );
    }

    return Card(
      child: Padding(
        padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
        child: Column(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: [
            Text(
              '${t('SCHEDULE.TITLE_PREFIX')} ${schedule.day} - ${schedule.doctor.title} '
              '${schedule.doctor.firstName} ${schedule.doctor.lastName}',
              style: Theme.of(context).textTheme.titleMedium,
            ),
            const SizedBox(height: 12),
            // DataTable: the Flutter Material equivalent of the HTML <table> of
            // Schedule.vue - unlike HTML, its rows must be
            // built explicitly in Dart through .map(...).toList()
            // (the equivalent, here again, of v-for="daySlot in
            // schedule.slots" :key="daySlot.slot.id" - the DataRow
            // needs no explicit "key" as in Vue.js/React: the
            // list is entirely rebuilt at each render, Flutter not
            // trying here to reuse existing rows).
            SingleChildScrollView(
              scrollDirection: Axis.horizontal,
              child: DataTable(
                columns: [
                  DataColumn(label: Text(t('SCHEDULE.COLUMN_SLOT'))),
                  DataColumn(label: Text(t('SCHEDULE.COLUMN_STATUS'))),
                  const DataColumn(label: Text('')),
                ],
                rows: schedule.slots.map((daySlot) {
                  final appointment = daySlot.appointment;
                  final slot = daySlot.slot;
                  return DataRow(
                    // slightly tinted background for a free slot - the
                    // counterpart of the "free-slot" CSS class on the Vue.js side.
                    color: appointment == null
                        ? WidgetStateProperty.all(Theme.of(context).colorScheme.surfaceContainerLow)
                        : null,
                    cells: [
                      DataCell(Text(
                        '${_formatTime(slot.startHour, slot.startMinute)} - '
                        '${_formatTime(slot.endHour, slot.endMinute)}',
                      )),
                      DataCell(
                        appointment == null
                            ? Chip(
                                label: Text(t('SCHEDULE.FREE')),
                                backgroundColor: Colors.green.shade100,
                              )
                            : Chip(
                                label: Text('${appointment.client?.title ?? ''} ${appointment.client?.firstName ?? ''} ${appointment.client?.lastName ?? ''}'),
                              ),
                      ),
                      DataCell(
                        // canEdit: false for a USER role (read-only)
                        canEdit
                            ? OutlinedButton(
                                onPressed: () => _onSlotClick(daySlot),
                                child: Text(appointment == null ? t('SCHEDULE.BOOK') : t('SCHEDULE.CANCEL_APPOINTMENT')),
                              )
                            : const SizedBox.shrink(),
                      ),
                    ],
                  );
                }).toList(),
              ),
            ),
          ],
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 43–57: [_formatTime(h, m)] and [_onSlotClick(daySlot)] — the latter distinguishes between an available slot ([onBook(...)]) and a booked slot ([onCancel(...)]) depending on whether [daySlot.appointment] is [null] or not, exactly the same logic as on the [Vue.js] side, but expressed purely in [Dart] rather than in [<template>].
  • Lines 96–137: [DataTable(columns: [...], rows: schedule.slots.map((daySlot) { ... }).toList())] — the [Material] equivalent of [<table>] [HTML] from [Schedule.vue]: its lines must be explicitly constructed via [.map(...).toList()].
  • Lines 108–110: [color: appointment == null ? WidgetStateProperty.all(Theme.of(context).colorScheme.surfaceContainerLow) : null,] — the counterpart to the ["free-slot"] [CSS] class on the [Vue.js] side: a background color applied conditionally to the entire line, here via a function rather than a named [CSS] class.

docs.title: 5.9.4. lib/features/booking_dialog/booking_dialog.dart
docs.text:
Porting of [src/app/features/booking-dialog/BookingDialog.vue]: a patient’s selection to reserve an available time slot—the file where the structural difference from [Vue.js] is most pronounced in this entire client.

// =========================================================================
// features/booking_dialog/booking_dialog.dart
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Port of src/app/features/booking-dialog/BookingDialog.vue (Vue.js
// client of this course): the (modal) window used to choose a
// patient to book a free slot.
//
// IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE with Vue.js (and with the three other
// widgets of lib/features/): BookingDialog.vue is a component ALWAYS
// PRESENT in the tree, whose [open] prop (a boolean held by
// App.vue) merely drives the display (v-if="open") - EXACTLY the same
// choice as the Angular and React clients of this course, motivated by the concern
// of preventing Vue.js and Bootstrap's JavaScript from fighting over the
// same piece of information ("is the modal open?").
//
// Flutter does not have this problem: a dialog box IS NOT a widget
// that is conditionally shown or hidden in the tree, but a REAL
// PAGE, pushed onto the navigation stack (the Navigator) when it is
// opened, with showDialog(...) - and automatically popped when it is
// closed. So there is here NEITHER an "open: bool" state to hold in the
// parent widget (see lib/app.dart, which has no field equivalent to
// slotBeingBooked on the Vue.js side), NOR "confirm"/"close" events to
// emit: showDialog(...) returns a Future that completes with the
// value passed to Navigator.pop(...) - null if the user closed
// without choosing, the id of the chosen patient otherwise. It is the
// CALLING widget (lib/app.dart) that awaits this Future to know what
// to do next - a complete reversal of the direction of communication
// compared with the two Vue.js events.
// =========================================================================

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:provider/provider.dart';

import '../../core/i18n/translations_service.dart';
import '../../core/models/appointment_models.dart';

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
// helper function: opens the dialog box and returns the id of the
// chosen patient (or null if the user cancelled/closed without choosing).
// It is THIS function that lib/app.dart calls - never directly the
// constructor of _BookingDialogContent below.
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------
Future<int?> openBookingDialog({
  required BuildContext context,
  required SlotJson slot,
  required List<Client> clients,
}) {
  return showDialog<int>(
    context: context,
    builder: (_) => _BookingDialogContent(slot: slot, clients: clients),
  );
}

class _BookingDialogContent extends StatefulWidget {
  final SlotJson slot;
  final List<Client> clients;

  const _BookingDialogContent({required this.slot, required this.clients});

  @override
  State<_BookingDialogContent> createState() => _BookingDialogContentState();
}

class _BookingDialogContentState extends State<_BookingDialogContent> {
  int? _selectedClientId;

  void _onConfirmClick() {
    final clientId = _selectedClientId;
    if (clientId == null) {
      return;
    }
    // Navigator.pop(context, clientId): closes the dialog box AND
    // passes clientId as the result of the Future returned by
    // openBookingDialog(...) - the equivalent, in a single call, of
    // emit('confirm', { clientId }) FOLLOWED by the closing (implicit,
    // driven by the parent through [open]) on the Vue.js side.
    Navigator.pop(context, clientId);
  }

  void _onCloseClick() {
    // Navigator.pop(context) without a second argument: the Future returned by
    // openBookingDialog(...) completes with null - the equivalent of
    // emit('close') on the Vue.js side.
    Navigator.pop(context);
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    final t = context.watch<TranslationsService>().t;
    final slot = widget.slot;

    // AlertDialog: the Material widget dedicated to dialog boxes -
    // already provides, on its own, the darkened background (the equivalent of the
    // .modal-backdrop placed "by hand" on the Vue.js side) and the
    // standard closing behavior (tap outside the box, Escape key
    // on desktop/web) - a behavior that the Vue.js client had to
    // recreate itself, Bootstrap handling only part of it automatically.
    return AlertDialog(
      title: Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.TITLE')),
      content: Column(
        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
        children: [
          Text(
            '${t('BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT_FROM')} ${slot.startHour}:${slot.startMinute.toString().padLeft(2, '0')} '
            '${t('BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT_TO')} ${slot.endHour}:${slot.endMinute.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}',
          ),
          const SizedBox(height: 16),
          DropdownButtonFormField<int>(
            decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: t('BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL')),
            value: _selectedClientId,
            hint: Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CHOOSE_PATIENT')),
            items: widget.clients
                .map(
                  (client) => DropdownMenuItem(
                    value: client.id,
                    child: Text('${client.title} ${client.firstName} ${client.lastName}'),
                  ),
                )
                .toList(),
            onChanged: (id) => setState(() => _selectedClientId = id),
          ),
        ],
      ),
      actions: [
        TextButton(onPressed: _onCloseClick, child: Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CANCEL'))),
        FilledButton(
          onPressed: _selectedClientId == null ? null : _onConfirmClick,
          child: Text(t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CONFIRM')),
        ),
      ],
    );
  }
}

Let’s comment on this code:

  • lines 16–28: The header comment summarizes the most significant structural difference in this file—[BookingDialog.vue] is a component ALWAYS PRESENT in the tree, whose display alone is controlled by a Boolean property ([open], held by [App.vue]); a dialog box [Flutter], on the other hand, is NEVER present until it is explicitly opened with [showDialog(...)]—a true page stacked on the navigation stack, automatically unstacked when closed.
  • Lines 43–52: [Future<int?> openBookingDialog({...}) { return showDialog<int>(context: context, builder: (_) => _BookingDialogContent(...)); }]—the function called by [lib/app.dart]; its return type ([Future<int?>]) already indicates that IT will eventually return either the ID of the selected patient or [null].
  • Lines 67–77: [Navigator.pop(context, clientId);] — closes the dialog box AND returns [clientId] as the result of [Future], which was returned by [openBookingDialog(...)] - the equivalent, in a single call, of what [emit('confirm', { clientId })] FOLLOWED by a parent-driven closure did TOGETHER on the [Vue.js] side.
  • Lines 80–84: [Navigator.pop(context);] without a second argument—[Future] then ends with [null], which is equivalent to [emit('close')] on the [Vue.js] side. It is [lib/app.dart] ([_onBookingRequest(...)]) that [await]s the [Future] and decides what to do depending on whether the result is [null] or not — a complete reversal of the communication direction compared to the two Vue.js events.
